title: Dragon-Kiln Fire Keeper
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Uncle Chaiyao（Uncle Chaiyao past fifty, graying short braid, earth-red coarse jacket and black apron, cuffs stained with porcelain clay, hands mapped with burn scars, gaze steady as fire） bends into the dragon-kiln chamber（An earth-red dragon-kiln chamber built against the mountain, fire mouth breathing orange flame, kiln walls thick with kiln sweat）; the dragon-kiln saggers（A stack of refractory dragon-kiln saggers, earth-yellow bodies intact, rims stacked tight, thin glaze on the inner walls） stand neatly stacked in the firelight.

A row of five fire-watch cups（A row of five fire-watch cups hung on iron nails by the kiln-chamber peephole, rims streaked with glaze tears） hangs by the kiln-chamber peephole; Uncle Chaiyao wipes ash from each rim.

Two kiln-opening gongs（Two kiln-opening gongs hung under the kiln-shed beams, faces chiselled with the character 'Dragon', trembling lightly when the wind rises） hang under the kiln-shed beams; Uncle Chaiyao reaches to make the faces tremble lightly.
Uncle Chaiyao circles the dragon-kiln saggers, checking whether the rims stack tight.
Through the peephole Uncle Chaiyao watches the darkening sky outside the kiln.
Intact dragon-kiln saggers quietly hold glazed blanks deep in the chamber.
Uncle Chaiyao sits by the fuel mouth and dozes in the firelight.
Night wind pours into the kiln mouth; Uncle Chaiyao tightens the collar of his coarse jacket.

Uncle Chaiyao opens the kiln-temperature ledger（A thread-bound kiln-temperature ledger, cover marked 'Dragon Kiln No. 3', pages filled in vermilion with fuel-feed times and fire color） and notes this shift's fuel-feed time in vermilion.
Uncle Chaiyao draws a fire-color curve in the kiln-temperature ledger.
Uncle Chaiyao closes the kiln-temperature ledger and sets it back in the clay jar by the peephole.
Heat from the dragon-kiln saggers reddens Uncle Chaiyao's cheek.
Uncle Chaiyao gently wipes sweat and ash from his brow with a damp cloth.

In the morning blank-drying yard（A cobble blank-drying yard outside the kiln mouth, half-dry pottery blanks on bamboo racks, sun shadows moving） Uncle Chaiyao greets young Dandelion（Young Dandelion: a lean wheel-throwing apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, yellow cloth scarf at the nape, gray-brown work clothes, blue cord on the left wrist, eyes clear and stubborn） pushing the green Mud Snail（A green-lacquered two-wheel plank cart, sides painted white with 'Mud Snail', bed lined with straw mats for hauling blanks） in.
Dandelion steadies Mud Snail and lifts half-dry blanks from the cart bed onto the bamboo racks.

Uncle Chaiyao points to the three pyrometric cones（Three triangular pyrometric cones set by hardness in a refractory-clay seat beside the saggers） beside the saggers and teaches Dandelion to read hardness and bending order.
Dandelion squats on the cobbles and curiously touches knife marks on the half-dry blanks.
Uncle Chaiyao points to the ridge and explains to Dandelion how the dragon kiln draws draft.
Dandelion looks back at the parked Mud Snail, eyes full of longing.
They lean side by side against the bamboo racks, listening to the deep roar from the kiln mouth.

In the glaze dark room（A narrow glaze dark room beside the kiln, clay jars in rows, air smelling of sulfur and plant ash） Aheng（Young Aheng: face closely resembling Dandelion's, but indigo cloth scarf, a pottery-bead bracelet on the right wrist, manner more playful） in an indigo cloth scarf looks back from behind the clay jars.
Aheng stirs ash glaze with a wooden stick; the pottery-bead bracelet on her right wrist lightly taps the jar rim.
Aheng taps a formula on the dark-room wall with a finger and smiles playfully.
Aheng carries a glaze box through the shadows of the glaze dark room.
Sulfur smell thickens; Aheng stops to listen to cracking sounds in the kiln chamber.
In the blank-drying yard Dandelion and Aheng stand side by side—one yellow cloth scarf, one indigo.
Dandelion hands a pyrometric cone to Aheng; they smile at each other.
Aheng straightens Dandelion's yellow cloth scarf; they walk slowly along the bamboo racks.
Dandelion and Aheng part at the west end of the blank-drying yard and walk opposite ways.
Dust rises; the sisters' backs—one yellow, one blue—gradually draw apart.
On a night months later Uncle Chaiyao alone watches fire in the dragon-kiln chamber; the dragon-kiln saggers quietly hold heat.

Uncle Chaiyao opens the kiln-temperature ledger（The same ledger blackened by kiln smoke, cover curling, writing blurred into ash blotches） and finds the cover already blackened by kiln smoke, writing blurred into ash blotches.
Uncle Chaiyao wipes kiln sweat condensed on the dragon-kiln sagger rims.
Through the peephole Uncle Chaiyao watches the pitch-black ridge outside the kiln.
Outlines of the dragon-kiln saggers slowly appear in the firelight.
Uncle Chaiyao tucks the stained kiln-temperature ledger into the clay jar and sighs.
Through the turning seasons Uncle Chaiyao day after day feeds fuel into the dragon-kiln chamber.
On another snow night Uncle Chaiyao wraps his apron tight and keeps watch by the dragon-kiln saggers.
At spring kiln repair Uncle Chaiyao patches refractory clay inside the chamber.
At high summer noon Uncle Chaiyao wipes the kiln-shed iron sheet baked hot by the sun.
In endless autumn rain heat from the dragon-kiln saggers steams in the damp air.
On another New Year's Eve Uncle Chaiyao alone keeps watch in the dragon-kiln chamber until dawn.
On a small-kiln test-fire night Uncle Chaiyao clears ash two hours early.
On a full-kiln night Uncle Chaiyao packs refractory wool tight into sagger seams.
When a cold snap hits Uncle Chaiyao hangs wind-break grass curtains on the kiln door.
Around Qingming Uncle Chaiyao sweeps pine needles and broken blanks from the blank-drying yard.
In plum-rain season Uncle Chaiyao repeatedly checks the kiln-door sealing clay for leaks.
At the first frost of early winter Uncle Chaiyao's white breath drifts under the fire-watch cups.
For three rainless nights in a row Uncle Chaiyao keeps the fuel-feed rhythm razor-tight.
One night kiln pressure spikes suddenly; Uncle Chaiyao has to half-open the kiln door to vent.
When the fire turns blue-green Uncle Chaiyao quickly adds pine fuel.
At three in the morning Uncle Chaiyao drinks ice-cold tea from a coarse porcelain bowl.
By the peephole he sorts the pyrometric-cone numbers.
The kiln-opening gongs tremble lightly in the wind; Uncle Chaiyao looks up to listen.
As the sky pales Uncle Chaiyao records last night's final fuel feed.
Before sealing the kiln he takes one last look at the intact rims of the dragon-kiln saggers.
At dawn Uncle Chaiyao patrols the blank-drying yard; green Mud Snail rests by the bamboo racks.
Uncle Chaiyao crouches to check whether Mud Snail's wheels and straw mats are damp.
Uncle Chaiyao walks to the saggers; those three pyrometric cones still stand neatly inserted.

A strange earth-yellow donkey cart（A strange earth-yellow donkey cart loaded with firewood bundles, no Mud Snail lettering anywhere—not the same as Mud Snail） rolls past the kiln-mouth road, bed loaded with firewood bundles—not Mud Snail.
Uncle Chaiyao stands on the cobbles and records last night's kiln-pressure peak.
Uncle Chaiyao re-covers the half-dry blanks with rainproof oilcloth.
Distant mountain mist withdraws, revealing deeper terrace shadows.
Kiln pressure surges; the dragon-kiln chamber shudders in the roar; the dragon-kiln saggers shake hard.
Flame tongues lick the kiln wall; Uncle Chaiyao rushes to the pressure-vent gate.
A sharp crack—the dragon-kiln saggers（The same stack of dragon-kiln saggers bursts apart, shards scattered, rim gaps jagged） burst apart, shards flying.
Outside the kiln mouth green Mud Snail jolts hard in the panicked push and pull.
A sideways tip splits Mud Snail（The green plank cart's side boards split and overturn, wheels come off—wreckage that can no longer carry blanks）'s side boards and overturns it; the wheels come off.
In the chamber Uncle Chaiyao lunges at the remaining dragon-kiln saggers, clamping down hard on the few unburst ones.
The day after the kiln burst Uncle Chaiyao stands in the dragon-kiln chamber staring at the burst dragon-kiln saggers.
Uncle Chaiyao traces a sagger gap with his finger, expression dark.
On a note beside the kiln-temperature ledger Uncle Chaiyao records the date Mud Snail overturned.
An old photo of Mud Snail hangs on the kiln-shed wall; Uncle Chaiyao gazes at it a long time.
Uncle Chaiyao takes one of the five fire-watch cups from the wall and sits alone in the glaze-tear reflection.
Damaged dragon-kiln saggers still litter the chamber center, gaps glaring.
Weeks later Uncle Chaiyao brings refractory clay and a seam knife and begins rebuilding the dragon-kiln saggers.

From a wooden crate Uncle Chaiyao takes a stack of small test saggers（A waist-high stack of small test saggers, shaped much like the dragon-kiln saggers but thinner and smaller—not that stack in the chamber）—much like the dragon-kiln saggers but smaller.
Carefully Uncle Chaiyao patches seams, rebuilds, and restacks the kiln.

The last repair scar is smoothed; the dragon-kiln saggers（The dragon-kiln saggers restored after rebuilding and seam-patching, dark repair scars on the bodies, distinct from the first intact state） enter the rebuilt-repaired state.
The repaired dragon-kiln saggers hold blanks again; Uncle Chaiyao looks on with relief.

A green-shell plank cart（A brand-new green-shell motor plank cart, sides sprayed with 'Green Shell', no Mud Snail mark—utterly different from Mud Snail） rolls into the blank-drying yard—nothing like the already overturned Mud Snail.

The glaze-works supervisor Old Min（Old Min, glaze-works supervisor past fifty, graying short braid and earth-red jacket similar in build to Uncle Chaiyao, but with an enamel work badge on his chest） steps onto the blank-drying yard and talks beside Uncle Chaiyao; the two look similar in build.
Old Min points at the green-shell plank cart and explains the new blank-haul schedule to Uncle Chaiyao.
The green-shell plank cart drives off; Uncle Chaiyao alone watches from the blank-drying yard.
Wind flaps the schedule sheet Old Min left behind.

Outside the kiln mouth comes neighbor-village youth Maimiao（Neighbor-village youth Maimiao, fourteen or fifteen, yellow cloth scarf, at a glance like young Dandelion, but no blue cord on the left wrist, shy-eyed） in a yellow cloth scarf—at a glance somewhat like young Dandelion.
Maimiao tries carrying blanks; Uncle Chaiyao shakes his head—he is not Dandelion after all.
Maimiao leaves the blank-drying yard with an empty basket; his back fades along the kiln-mouth road.

At dusk years later Uncle Chaiyao（The same Uncle Chaiyao after burns: right-arm bandage, limping on a bamboo crutch, still in that ash-stained earth-red coarse jacket） with a right-arm bandage leans on a bamboo crutch outside the earth-red dragon-kiln chamber.
Uncle Chaiyao leans on the crutch and looks up at the towering kiln ridge, gaze distant.
Under the kiln-shed beams those two kiln-opening gongs tremble lightly in the wind; Uncle Chaiyao stops on his crutch to listen.
Uncle Chaiyao presses a palm to the cold kiln-head stone pillar as if saying goodbye.
He slowly sits on the blank-drying yard's stone steps, limping leg stretched straight.

By day adult Dandelion（Adult Dandelion: a broad-shouldered thrower in her twenties, still with yellow cloth scarf and blue cord on the left wrist, manner steady） returns along the kiln-mouth road and hurries toward the dragon-kiln chamber.
At the kiln head Dandelion reunites with cane-leaning Uncle Chaiyao; they embrace.
By the kiln-shed narrow cot Dandelion holds Uncle Chaiyao's burn-scarred but ice-cold hand.
Uncle Chaiyao（Uncle Chaiyao lies still with eyes closed on a narrow cot in the kiln shed, face peaceful, breath gone）'s breath grows weak; at last he closes his eyes and passes away.
Dandelion gently sets Uncle Chaiyao's fuel hook back beside the cot.
Behind the kiln-shed door Uncle Chaiyao's earth-red coarse jacket still hangs; Dandelion reaches to stroke it gently.

By the kiln-head stone pillar adult Dandelion stands before a newly nailed kiln-god bronze plaque（A kiln-god bronze plaque nailed to the kiln-head stone pillar, carved with Uncle Chaiyao's name and the kiln-opening year, edges mottled with verdigris）.
Dandelion's fingertip traces Uncle Chaiyao's name carved on the kiln-god bronze plaque.
Wind rises; kiln-opening gongs tremble faintly in the distance; Dandelion lifts her head.

Adult Aheng（Adult Aheng: face closely resembling adult Dandelion's, still indigo cloth scarf and pottery-bead bracelet, glaze box over the shoulder） arrives from the neighboring village and tightly embraces Dandelion at the kiln head.
Dandelion and Aheng stand side by side by the kiln-head stone pillar—one quiet, one playful.
They look at each other in silence, watching faces alike yet different.
Aheng opens the glaze box, then quietly closes it, only standing with her sister.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth touching knife marks on half-dry blanks on the cobbles appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the chamber a stack of earth-yellow saggers first takes glazed blanks.
Flashback to that year's glaze dark room—the indigo-scarfed figure with a pottery-bead bracelet slips past.
Again that row of five old porcelain cups streaked with glaze tears by the peephole appears.
Back to that cobble blank-drying yard of first meeting, bamboo racks aslant as before.
Dandelion opens again that smoke-stained kiln-temperature ledger and walks into the dragon-kiln chamber.
Beside the saggers those three pyrometric cones still stand neatly inserted.
Dandelion takes over fire watch of the dragon-kiln saggers; heat surges again toward the kiln mouth.
Outside the peephole the ridge outline grows clear in morning light.
